description: Two vertically stacked mechanical-property panels, each with a broken ordinate: an upper strength sub-plot (MPa, ticks 500-1300 with a break) and a lower toughness sub-plot (J/cm2, ticks 0-200 with a break) sharing a right-hand axis labelled "TE or δ" (%, 0-80). (a) Fe-30Mn-xAl-(0.85,0.95)C versus Al (wt%), x-axis 3-11; the legend defines solid line = 0.95%C and dashed line = 0.85%C, while filled triangles mark UTS and open triangles mark YS; curves are labelled UTS, YS, E_CUN, TE and δ. UTS and YS both rise with Al, steeply above about 7 wt%, and the 0.95%C curves lie above the 0.85%C ones; E_CUN and TE pass through a maximum at intermediate Al (roughly 5-6 wt%) and drop at high Al; δ points appear only near Al ≈ 8-9.5 wt% at small values at the bottom of the right axis. (b) Fe-30Mn-9Al-xC versus C (wt%), x-axis 0.3-1.3; per the caption the solid curves are aged 550 °C/16 h and the dashed curve is water quenched from 1050 °C. UTS and YS increase monotonically with C; E_CUN and TE both peak near 0.7 wt% C then decline; δ falls from about 40% to zero by ≈0.8 wt% C. The panels jointly show that Al and C shift the strength-toughness balance.

subfigures.description: Strength (MPa, 500-1300, broken) and toughness (J/cm2, 0-200, broken) versus Al (wt%) 3-11 for Fe-30Mn-xAl-(0.85,0.95)C; legend: solid = 0.95%C, dashed = 0.85%C; filled triangles = UTS, open triangles = YS; curves labelled UTS, YS, E_CUN, TE, δ; right-hand axis 'TE or δ (%)' 0-80. UTS/YS rise with Al (steep above ~7 wt%), E_CUN and TE peak at intermediate Al then fall, δ small and only at high Al.

Strength (MPa, 500-1300, broken) and toughness (J/cm2, 0-200, broken) versus C (wt%) 0.3-1.3 for Fe-30Mn-9Al-xC; solid = aged 550 °C/16 h, dashed = water quenched from 1050 °C (per caption). UTS and YS increase monotonically with C; E_CUN and TE peak near 0.7 wt% C; δ decreases from about 40% to zero by ~0.8 wt% C.

observations.observation: Panel (a) plots Fe-30Mn-xAl-(0.85,0.95)C with Al (wt%) on the x-axis over 3-11 wt%; the upper sub-plot is strength (MPa, 500-1300, broken axis) and the lower sub-plot is toughness (J/cm2, 0-200, broken axis) with a right-hand axis labelled 'TE or δ (%)' 0-80.
The legend in (a) defines the solid curve as 0.95%C and the dashed curve as 0.85%C; filled triangles mark UTS and open triangles mark YS.
In (a) both UTS and YS increase with increasing Al, with the steep rise occurring above about 7 wt% Al, and the 0.95%C curves lie above the corresponding 0.85%C curves.
In (a) the E_CUN and TE curves pass through a maximum at intermediate Al (roughly 5-6 wt%) and then decrease towards the highest Al contents.
In (a) the δ data points appear only at the highest Al contents (about 8-9.5 wt%) and sit low on the right-hand 'TE or δ (%)' axis.
Panel (b) plots Fe-30Mn-9Al-xC with C (wt%) on the x-axis over 0.3-1.3 wt%, using the same broken strength/toughness layout as (a).
In (b) UTS and YS increase monotonically with increasing C, and the YS curve rises steeply at C above roughly 0.8 wt%.
In (b) both E_CUN and TE peak near 0.7 wt% C and then decline at higher C.
In (b) the δ curve decreases from about 40% at low C to essentially zero near 0.8 wt% C.
The caption states that the (a) alloys were water quenched from 1150 °C and aged at 550 °C for 16 h, and that E_CUN is the impact energy measured from U-notch Charpy specimens.
The caption states that the (b) alloys were water quenched from 1050 °C (dashed curve) and aged at 550 °C for 16 h (solid curves), with data taken from Ref. [7].

The citing text states that alloys with intermediate Al concentrations (about 2-7%) do not offer improved tensile properties compared with the Al-free steel, whereas alloys containing Al > 7% and C > 0.7% can produce pronounced strengthening after aging through fine and dispersed κ-carbides.

The citing text states that an increase in C content increases strength, ductility and impact toughness up to about 0.7% C in the aged condition, while above about 0.7% C strength continues to increase but ductility and impact toughness decrease.
The citing text states that as Al exceeds 10%, δ-ferrite is introduced as a banded phase which further decreases plasticity and toughness and enhances anisotropy of the mechanical properties.
The citing text states that the increase in Al content from 7 to 11% gives an increase in the age-hardening effect while having less influence on the age-hardening kinetics.

unreadable_items: Exact data-point values are not printed in either panel; only axis tick positions and curve shapes are legible, so values are described by gridline position only.
Panel (a) contains two E_CUN-style curves (solid and dashed) whose individual curve-to-composition assignment relies on the line-style legend rather than a printed label.
